questions.q: What does an Athena external table actually store?
options: A compressed backup of the source database
No data at all — it's metadata pointing at an S3 location, format, and column definitions
Only the query results from the last SELECT run against it
A full copy of the underlying S3 data inside Athena
questions.explain: An external table is a Catalog entry describing where data lives and its shape — the same kind of entry a crawler would create.

questions.q: In a CREATE EXTERNAL TABLE statement, what does the LOCATION clause specify?
options: The name of the IAM role used to run the query
The AWS Region the query must run in
The Athena workgroup the table belongs to
The S3 prefix the table reads its underlying data from
questions.explain: LOCATION points the table at the S3 path where its data actually lives.

questions.q: Why must every column be explicitly typed when declaring a CSV-backed external table, but not necessarily for Parquet?
options: Parquet requires manual typing but CSV does not
CSV files are always smaller than Parquet files
CSV carries no embedded schema of its own, while Parquet files embed their schema
Athena cannot read CSV files under any circumstances
questions.explain: Parquet embeds schema in the file itself; CSV is untyped text, so the table definition must spell out every column's type.

questions.q: What determines the cost of the example SELECT query shown in this lesson?
options: The complexity of the GROUP BY clause alone, unrelated to data size
The bytes scanned in the S3 objects the raw.orders table points at
The number of rows returned to the client
A flat per-query fee regardless of data size
questions.explain: Consistent with Athena's pricing model, the query's cost is driven by how many bytes it scans in the underlying S3 data.

questions.q: What is a JSON SerDe used for in an external table definition?
options: Encrypting JSON data at rest in S3
Validating that JSON is syntactically well-formed before storage
Mapping JSON keys in the source files to table column names
Converting JSON files into Parquet automatically at query time
questions.explain: A SerDe (serializer/deserializer) is the logic that maps a file format's structure — like JSON keys — onto table columns.
